# Three CLIs, one question — the probe, 2026-09-13

## Access and confidence

One machine (Apple M4, 24 GB, macOS), one afternoon, this repository's root
as the working directory. Each command was run once, alone. The question
was read-only by construction and each agent was told so; no file changed.
Wall times include each tool's start-up. A sample of one.

The question, verbatim:

> Answer in at most two sentences, without editing anything: which files at
> the root of this repository (or in .claude/) are instructions for AI
> agents, and what is the one rule they most insist on?

The correct answer: the only such file is `.claude/skills/okf/SKILL.md`
(there is no `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` at this repository's root; the
`video/` projects carry both), and its rule is *run, do not quote* — derive
a figure by running the attested computation, never by copying it.

## Claude Code — 16 s, first try

```
claude -p "<question>" --permission-mode plan
```

Named the file and the rule ("get any figure from an attested computation
by running its executor and checking the run with its attester, never by
copying the number from an article, and say which trust tier the answer
rests on"). 16 s.

## Codex — refused, updated, 23 s

```
codex exec --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval never "<question>"
```

Two things went wrong on the first try, one mine. `--ask-for-approval` is
not an `exec` flag (it belongs to the interactive client). Without it:

```
ERROR: The 'gpt-6-astra' model requires a newer version of Codex. Please upgrade…
```

plus a logged failure to parse the model list (`unknown variant 'max'`).
`codex update` took 8 s (0.132.0 → 0.154.0). Then:

```
codex exec --sandbox read-only "<question>"
```

answered in 23 s, 12,119 tokens: the same file, the rule paraphrased as
"answer content questions from the okf/ bundle, respecting its trust
metadata and deriving computational figures through sanctioned, attested
runs."

## Antigravity CLI — refused four ways, then 54 s

| Attempt | Command / configuration | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `agy --print "<q>"` | "This version of Antigravity CLI is no longer supported. Please run agy update, /logout, then log in again." (`agy --version` said 1.0.0; `agy update` said 1.2.2 and already latest.) |
| 2 | `agy --print` after the update | "no output produced — a tool required the `command` permission that headless mode cannot prompt for, so it was auto-denied." 11 s. |
| 3 | `agy --sandbox --print` | Same denial. 9 s. `settings.json` was `{}`. |
| 4 | allow-rules `command(ls)`, `command(cat)`, `command(find)`, `command(grep)`, `command(rg)`, `command(head)`, `command(git status)`, `command(git log)` | Now denied on `read_file` — the working directory was not the workspace. 10 s. |
| 4b | the same, plus `--add-dir "$PWD"` | Worked for 36 s, then denied on a command outside the allow-list. |
| **5** | `enableTerminalSandbox: true`, `toolPermission: "proceed-in-sandbox"`, plus `--add-dir "$PWD"` | **Answered in 54 s**: the same file; "run, do not quote — requiring agents to answer from the okf/ bundle and derive figures by executing and attesting sanctioned computations rather than reading or quoting numbers off articles." Correct. |

The settings file was restored to `{}` afterwards. What attempt 5 is, in
the docs' terms: the OS sandbox (`sandbox-exec` on macOS) on, and the
permission setting under which "sandboxed commands run automatically, while
commands that need to run outside the sandbox still prompt for review."
It is the configuration the CLI's own sandbox page gives; nothing in the
error messages points to it — they suggest allow-rules or
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

## What the probe says

- All three agents found the same file and stated the same rule. On a
  read-only question of this size, the engines are not the variable.
- The variable is what each tool insists on before it will run: Claude
  nothing beyond a permission mode; Codex an update its own model demanded;
  Antigravity a permission configuration that its headless mode cannot ask
  for interactively and its errors do not name.
- 16 s, 23 s, 54 s — the first two comparable, the third with a sandbox
  around every command. None is a benchmark; all are "a question, a tool,
  an afternoon."
